# Frozen Zova correctness corpus

These are 30 complete function excerpts from Zova commit
`88197842e5a7b2d2477fc4e2c073c1f518817ba1`, licensed under MIT (see `LICENSE`).
They contain 46 labeled callable owners: 18 with matches and 28 with none.
There are 19 expected sites: 17 Rust clone calls and two Go launch statements.

`labels.json` records original file/line boundaries, snapshot SHA-256, owner
identity and byte ranges, counts, and exact evidence strings/ranges. Source in
`source/` is verbatim, including indentation; Go excerpts have `package zova`
and a blank line prepended so they parse as files. Imports and surrounding impl
blocks are not included. These are syntax fixtures, not independently buildable
programs. Ranges refer to the frozen excerpt, not the original whole file.

## How expectations were established

The implementing agent read each whole excerpt and selected exact clone strings
and Go statement boundaries independently of Badbox output. A text-offset
calculation converted those explicit annotations into byte ranges. The same
review labeled error-construction/status closures and the two Go goroutine
bodies as zero-match owners. This is agent-reviewed ground truth, not an
independent human audit and not labels generated by the scanner under test.

The regression validates every labeled evidence range against the frozen source,
then compares Badbox's compact owner ranges and exact counts at threshold zero.
Unexpected findings, missing findings, wrong ownership, and wrong counts fail.
Individual match ranges are no longer part of the scan transport. At threshold
one, only the Go outer function should be emitted. Zero-count owners are not
returned by the current API; their labels assert absence of findings, not
exported zero-count metrics.
An additional test concatenates the Rust excerpts into one syntax-only file and
translates the fixed offsets, checking that equal owners remain distinct by byte
range when they share a file.

Run after building the native addon:

```bash
bun test tests/zova-corpus.test.ts
```

No Zova checkout is required. Do not refresh expected output from a Badbox scan.
When adding a regression, inspect the source, record explicit expectations and
provenance, then run the comparison.

## Coverage and limits

- Includes all 17 clone-owning functions found in the selected Rust binding
  source roots, plus eight zero-clone functions. Borrowed vs owned APIs,
  repeated method names, FFI calls, closures, and early returns are represented.
- Includes the Go concurrency test plus four zero-spawn functions. The launch
  statements are inside loops; their anonymous bodies have zero nested launches.
- The Go finding is not evidence of a leak. The test does finite work and joins
  its goroutines. The Rust counts do not establish cloning cost or necessity.
- This is a small, selected corpus, not exhaustive repository-wide recall, type
  analysis, macro-expansion coverage, or a statistical false-positive estimate.
- Real examples here have at most two sites per owner; higher-count and other
  nesting behavior is covered by the separate synthetic fixtures.
